title: Nasal endoscopy
what: An ENT doctor looks inside your nose and the back of your nose with a thin tube that has a camera.
why: For a long-lasting runny or blocked nose, nosebleeds, snoring, possible polyps or adenoids, or after a nose injury.
duration: usually 5 to 10 minutes; the doctor tells you the result right away
tell_doctor: If you recently had nose surgery

prepare.title: Prep
prepare.text: Usually none. You can eat and drink.

prepare.title: Before the exam
prepare.text: Blow your nose. Do not use decongestant drops on your own before the exam, unless your doctor says so.

bring: Your referral, if you have one
Past sinus images and ENT reports
steps: You sit in a chair with your head tilted back a little
A spray or cotton with medicine is put in your nose to numb it and reduce swelling
After a few minutes, the doctor puts a thin tube into your nose
The nasal passages and the back of the nose are checked, with the image on a screen
feel: Coolness and numbness from the spray, sometimes a bitter taste in the throat
Pressure in the nose and an urge to sneeze
after: The numbness wears off in 15 to 30 minutes
You can go about your day right away
The doctor usually explains what they saw right away
red_flags: A nosebleed that does not stop within 15 to 20 minutes: call emergency services

faq.a: Usually not, since the nose is numbed. It feels unpleasant, but bearable.
Yes, there are thin tubes for children. Your child needs to sit still. A parent usually stays close.

reminders.text: Nasal endoscopy soon. Blow your nose before the visit and bring past images, if you have them.
